_comment: Weather aliases, written against the 8 distinct values Fish.weather actually
The wiki is inconsistent in two places and both matter: 'Rain' and 'Rainy' are
the same weather, and 'Storm' and 'Thunderstorm' are the same weather. Treating
either pair as distinct would split fish across two states, and the app would
tell someone a fish isn't biting when it is.
Note that 'Clear' never appears in this column — the wiki expresses it as 'Any'.
'Any' resolves to all six states and the build then intersects that with the
weather each season can physically have, so a summer window never claims snow.
_gameComment: The game does not name six weathers. `fiddle/weather.toml` declares four
classes — calm, inclement, heavy_inclement, special — and the season decides
what each one looks like. A fish whose weather is ['heavy_inclement'] bites in
a thunderstorm in fall and a blizzard in winter, and that is one rule, not two.
Three of the four map without argument. `special` is the one that is reasoned
rather than read: the game's own seasonal_counts give spring and fall 4-6
special days each and summer and winter none, and Wind is the only one of the
wiki's six that is left. That is a deduction from two sources agreeing, not a
fact either of them states, which is why it is written down here with the
reasoning attached instead of buried in a lookup table in the build.
Consequence worth knowing: this says wind cannot occur in summer or winter,
and SEASON_LEGAL_WEATHER currently allows it in all four. The narrower claim
is the game's; it is applied to game-sourced windows only, and the wiki-sourced
ones keep the broader mask until something settles it for them too.
